mainTopic: Using metal skewers (שפודין) and bed boards (ארוכות המטה) as סכך: how equal spaces can still give a kosher סוכה, and whether a broken bed frame counts as a כלי
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's case of a סוכה roofed with metal skewers (שפודין) that have spaces between them. The גמרא asks how the סוכה can be kosher if the spaces are exactly equal to the skewers. רבי אמי answers that the משנה means the spaces are slightly wider. רבא answers that even equal spaces are enough, because the kosher סכך is laid crosswise over the skewers and so covers more than the gaps. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's next case, roofing with the long boards of a bed. It suggests this supports רבי אמי בר טביומי, who rules that worn-out vessels are פסול as סכך. The proof is pushed off: following רבי חנן in the name of רבי, the משנה may mean a board with two legs still attached, which is still a complete כלי. Finally the גמרא asks where רבי חנן's statement was first taught and begins to quote that משנה, which appears on the next amud.

steps.title: But exact equality is possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that a סוכה roofed with skewers is kosher when the spaces between them equal the skewers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is possible to measure exactly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier answer that the משנה's כמותן (gaps equal to the skewers) only means roughly equal, because nobody measures exactly. If the gaps are exactly as wide as the skewers, the kosher and the פסול parts are equal, so how can the סוכה be kosher?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the סוכה is kosher when the space between the skewers is כמותן (equal to them). But the kosher סכך is supposed to be more than the פסול material. Exact equality is a real possibility, so the משנה's ruling needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to measure with exact precision
Metal skewers or spits (the פסול roofing in the משנה)

phrases.english: But it is possible to be precise!
phrases.notes: If the gaps can be made exactly equal to the skewers, kosher and פסול would be equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier answer (end of 15a) that the משנה's כמותן means only roughly equal (נכנס ויוצא), since people do not usually measure exactly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a סוכה with spaces equal to the skewers (כמותן) is kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exact equality can actually happen. In that case the kosher סכך is not more than the פסול, so the סוכה should not be kosher.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the spaces are slightly wider
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that the משנה means the spaces are a bit wider than the skewers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: It is a case where he makes the spaces wider.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question. The משנה is talking about a case where the gaps are a little wider than the skewers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אמי, the word כמותן is not exact. The kosher part must actually be bigger, so the gaps must be wider than the skewers. With exactly equal gaps, the סוכה would not be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he adds extra (makes the spaces wider)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
It is where he makes the spaces wider.
phrases.notes: The gaps are slightly wider than the skewers.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to slightly wider spaces
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to permit spaces that are exactly equal to the skewers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's case has spaces slightly wider than the skewers, so the kosher part is the majority.

steps.title: רבא: lay the kosher roofing across the skewers
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even with exactly equal spaces the סוכה is kosher, because the kosher סכך is laid crosswise over the skewers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it is where he does not make the spaces wider. If the skewers were placed lengthwise, he places the kosher roofing widthwise. If they were widthwise, he places it lengthwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. Even if the gaps are exactly equal, the kosher סכך is laid across the skewers, so it covers more than the skewers do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kosher סכך does not just drop into the gaps. It is laid in the opposite direction from the skewers, so it rests on top of them and sticks out past each gap. That means the kosher covering is larger than the gap, and it is the majority even though the gaps themselves equal the skewers. The משנה can therefore be read literally.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the הלכה that kosher must be more than פסול. He agrees with that. He only shows how the kosher part is more even when the gaps are equal.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it is where he does not make the spaces wider,
if the skewers were placed lengthwise —
he places the kosher roofing widthwise,
if widthwise — he places it lengthwise.
phrases.notes: Laid crosswise, the kosher roofing rests over the skewers and covers more than the gap.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּשֶׁאֵין מַעֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 1 that does not need רבי אמי's narrowing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method: placing the סכך crosswise makes the kosher part the majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Equal gaps mean the kosher and פסול parts are equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Crosswise placement makes the kosher covering larger than the gaps, so even equal gaps produce a kosher סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: רבי אמי says the gaps are wider than the skewers. רבא says equal gaps are enough because the kosher סכך is laid across the skewers.

steps.title: Next phrase in the משנה: the long boards of a bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: roofing with the long boards of a bed is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or with the long boards of the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, a סוכה roofed with the long side-boards of a bed. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא will try to prove something from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that roofing with a bed's long boards is פסול. A bed is a כלי, and כלים cannot be used as סכך. The question will be whether a board separated from the bed still counts as a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: The long side-boards of a bed frame

phrases.english: Or with the long boards of the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roofing with the long boards of a bed is פסול.

steps.title: Suggested support for רבי אמי בר טביומי: worn vessels are invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה proves רבי אמי בר טביומי's rule that roofing with worn-out vessels is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבי אמי בר טביומי? For רבי אמי בר טביומי said: If he roofed it with worn-out vessels, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a proof. A board taken off a bed seems to be a broken piece of a כלי, and the משנה still calls it פסול, which would match רבי אמי בר טביומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי בר טביומי holds that broken, worn vessels are פסול for סכך even though they are no longer complete כלים, because they once were. A loose bed board looks like exactly that kind of broken piece. So the משנה's ruling would seem to support him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him? (opens a suggested proof)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רבי אמי בר טביומי here with רבי אמי in step 2. They are different people discussing different topics.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports
Rabbi Ami bar Tavyomei,
as Rabbi Ami bar Tavyomei said:
If he roofed it with worn-out vessels — it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר טַבְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה phrase quoted in step 4 as proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי בר טביומי's rule that worn-out vessels are פסול as סכך
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the long boards of a bed (seemingly broken parts of a כלי) are פסול

steps.title: Rejected: the board still has two legs attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the משנה means a board with two legs still attached, which is still a complete כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רבי חנן said in the name of רבי: a long board with two legs, or a short board with two legs. Here too: a long board with two legs, or a short board with two legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה may be talking about a bed board that still has two legs attached, which is still a usable bed and not a broken piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using רבי חנן's statement in the name of רבי, the גמרא shows that a board with two legs can lean against a wall and still work as a bed. Such a piece is still a full כלי, so its פסול says nothing about truly worn-out vessels. The proof for רבי אמי בר טביומי falls away, but his rule itself is not disproved.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's bed boards are פסול because they may still be a complete כלי (a board with two legs). So the משנה does not prove רבי אמי בר טביומי's rule about worn-out vessels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic move: a proof is rejected by narrowing the case, without disproving the opinion it was meant to support.

phrases.english: It is like what Rabbi Chanan said in the name of Rabbi:
phrases.notes: Said originally about when a broken bed can still become טמא.

phrases.english: with a long board and two legs,
with a short board and two legs.
Here too:
with a long board and two legs,
with a short board and two legs.
phrases.notes: Such a piece still works as a bed when leaned against a wall, so it is a full כלי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. רבי אמי בר טביומי's rule itself is left standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the bed boards were broken pieces. They may still be attached to two legs and so still be a complete כלי.

steps.title: Where was רבי חנן's statement originally said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the teaching of רבי חנן in the name of רבי was first said, and begins to answer that it was said on a certain משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where was the statement that רבי חנן said in the name of רבי originally said? It was said on this משנה that we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where a statement of רבי חנן, quoted in the name of רבי, was first taught. It starts to answer by saying 'on this משנה', which sets up the quote of that משנה on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Statements of אמוראים were usually said as comments on a specific משנה or ברייתא. To understand a statement properly, the גמרא first finds its original setting. This line does not argue anything yet. It only points us to the source text that will explain the statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Where was it said? Asks for the original setting of a statement
On this that we learned. Introduces the משנה the statement was said on

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge. The גמרא is only finding where the statement was first said. The real content comes when the משנה is quoted on the next amud.

phrases.english: Where was it stated
phrases.notes: The גמרא is just asking where this was first said, not challenging it.

phrases.english: that which Rabbi Chanan said in the name of Rabbi?
On this that we learned in a mishna:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (for the closing words אַהָא דִּתְנַן, which begin the answer)
steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא אִיתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי חָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After pushing off the proof by reading the משנה as a board with two legs still attached (step 6), the גמרא turns to the original setting of רבי חנן's statement in the name of רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original משנה on which רבי חנן's statement in the name of רבי was taught.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was said on a משנה. The answer is introduced with אַהָא דִּתְנַן, and the משנה itself is quoted on the next amud.
